title: Delta and Island: Bangladesh and Sri Lanka
description: Two schematic panels. A Bengal Delta where the Padma, Jamuna and Meghna rivers meet, with a monsoon slider that floods the lowest land first (illustrative; presets match the documented average of about 21% and the more than two-thirds flooded in 1998). Beside it, a stylized island of Sri Lanka with central highlands and tappable cards for Jaffna, Anuradhapura, Kandy, Sri Pada, Colombo and Galle.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Geography
Bangladesh
Sri Lanka
Rivers and floods
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Explain how the Bengal Delta's rivers and monsoon floods shape life in Bangladesh.
Describe how Sri Lanka's central highlands, coasts and ancient capitals are arranged on the island.
Compare how water and land shape the two countries.
prerequisites: Knowing the eight countries of South Asia and the monsoon (Chapter 1)
Knowing that Bangladesh became independent in 1971 (Chapter 4)
keyQuestions: Why does so much of Bangladesh flood each year?
How can floods be both harmful and helpful?
Where are Sri Lanka's highlands, ports and ancient capitals?
misconceptions: Bangladesh is mostly desert or dry.
Sri Lanka is part of India.
All flooding is a disaster with no benefit.
dataSources: Floods in Bangladesh (average 21% flooded; over two-thirds in 1998; about 80% of streamflow from outside the country): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floods_in_Bangladesh
